boundaries.before: A safe in-crate caller could fabricate any pointer, including one that is not NUL-terminated or does not outlive the owner. The stored coordinate then reached the allocator seam at release/growth, where an installed hook or failure diagnostic may read it as a C string. Current call sites were static, but the coordinate was not inexpressible.
boundaries.after: OwnedBuf stores `file: SeamFile`. Both safe constructors take `SeamFile`; the raw pointer is derived with `file.as_ptr()` only at the CRYPTO_malloc/CRYPTO_free/CRYPTO_realloc/CRYPTO_clear_realloc call. Safe callers can only supply `SeamFile::new(&'static CStr)` or `SeamFile::NULL`.
boundaries.mechanism: ELIMINATED: a non-NUL-terminated or short-lived coordinate is no longer expressible through a safe constructor; the static-lifetime precondition is carried by the type.

boundaries.after: Pass `SeamFile::new(F_INT_FILE)` / `SeamFile::new(F_STRING_FILE)`. Both constants are `&'static CStr`, so the constructor's static-lifetime requirement is checked by the compiler.
boundaries.mechanism: RELOCATED to the typed call; no dynamic coordinate exists, so no `unsafe fn ..._dynamic` route was added and `SeamFile::from_static_ptr` was not used.
